courses.prompt: Your soup is served. Which utensil will you reach for?
courses.hint: Choose a utensil that can hold the broth.
courses.explanation: Use the spoon for soup. Sip quietly from its side.
courses.subtitle: A warm beginning
courses.description: Lobster bisque, finished with crème fraîche and chives.
courses.image_alt: A bowl of lobster bisque with an herb garnish

courses.prompt: Which utensil will you use to bring a bite of burrata to your mouth?
courses.hint: Use the utensil with tines to lift a bite.
courses.explanation: Use your fork to bring the burrata and tomatoes to your mouth.
courses.subtitle: From the garden
courses.description: Burrata with heirloom tomatoes, fresh basil, and aged balsamic.
courses.image_alt: Burrata served over tomatoes with herbs

courses.prompt: Your steak needs cutting. Touch only the utensil you would use to cut a bite.
courses.hint: You need a cutting edge for this step. Select just that utensil.
courses.explanation: Cut a bite with your knife while steadying the steak with your fork.
courses.subtitle: The centerpiece
courses.description: Filet mignon with a red wine reduction and potato purée.
courses.image_alt: Grilled filet steak on a white plate with sauce

courses.subtitle: Something sweet
courses.description: Dark chocolate torte with raspberry coulis, to close the evening.
courses.prompt: Which utensil will you use for a bite of torte?
courses.hint: Use the utensil with tines to separate and lift a small bite.
courses.explanation: Use a fork to separate and lift a small bite of torte.
courses.image_alt: A slice of chocolate torte with cream on a white plate
